title: Heron's jet vs head (Torricelli, and what the nozzle costs)
description: Torricelli: water leaving a vessel under a head H can rise H again, v²/2g = H. Raise the drive slowly so the head sweeps from a few centimetres to its ceiling, and plot the jet's ideal height v²/2g against the head. It is a straight line through the origin — but its slope is 0.12, not 1: this nozzle's discharge coefficient (0.35) leaves the jet C_d² of the head, and pipe friction takes about another 2 %. On WebGPU with the liquid solver running, heronJetHeightM is the height of the simulated jet read back from the liquid, to compare with the ideal one; it lags the plant, because the liquid is shown at one sixth speed. Without a liquid solver it reads 0, 'not measured'. Simulated, not metrology.
